relevance_reason: Reports patients with axonal sensorimotor neuropathy caused by homozygous MPV17 variants without hepatocerebral involvement, which is the CMT2EE phenotype.

findings.statement: Baumann et al. (2019) described 5 patients from 2 unrelated families who had juvenile- or adult-onset sensorimotor axonal neuropathy without hepatocerebral involvement.
quotes: Here, we describe five additional patients from two unrelated families with sensorimotor axonal neuropathy without hepatocerebral affection caused by homozygous MPV17 variants.

findings.statement: In affected members of 1 of the 2 families with axonal sensorimotor neuropathy, Baumann et al. (2019) found the previously reported MPV17 c.122G>A (p.Arg41Gln) variant in the homozygous state.
quotes: Patients of the first family carried the known c.122G>A variant
caused by homozygous MPV17 variants

findings.statement: In affected members of the second family with axonal sensorimotor neuropathy, Baumann et al. (2019) found a novel homozygous MPV17 c.376-9T>G near-splice variant, which was shown to cause an in-frame deletion of 11 amino acids.
quotes: affected individuals of the second family had a novel c.376-9T>G near-splice variant, which was shown to result in an in-frame deletion of 11 amino acids

variants.consequence: splice site; in-frame deletion of 11 amino acids

relevance_reason: Reports two unrelated Korean families with axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy (CMT2-like) without hepatoencephalopathy caused by homozygous MPV17 p.R41Q mutation, with functional studies.

findings.statement: Choi et al. (2015) reported a 34-year-old Korean woman (patient 1, family FC26), born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents, with normal early motor milestones who first noticed distal lower limb weakness at 9 years of age and walked with short leg braces from age 12. At 34 years she had distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly in the lower limbs, severe atrophy of intrinsic hand, foot and calf muscles, flexion deformities of interphalangeal joints, ankle joint deformity, scoliosis, vibration and position sense more disturbed than pain and touch, and absent knee and ankle jerks. She had no growth retardation, gastrointestinal dysmotility, hepatomegaly, cognitive impairment, ophthalmoplegia, corneal scarring, or hypoglycemic attacks; serum lactate was mildly elevated (2.1 mmol/L) with normal liver enzymes, glucose and pyruvate.
quotes: At 9 years of age, she first noticed muscle weakness of the distal lower limbs. She began to walk with short leg braces at 12 years of age.

Bilateral, severe atrophic changes of the intrinsic hand, foot and calf muscles, and flexion deformities of interphalangeal joints were noted (Fig. 2a-c). Ankle joint deformity and scoliosis was observed although she was able to walk with orthopedic assistance.

However, she did not present any other clinical presentations of NNH, such as growth retardation, gastrointestinal dysmotility, hepatomegaly, cognitive impairment, ophthalmoplegia, corneal scarring or hypoglycemic attacks.

findings.statement: Choi et al. (2015) reported a 22-year-old Korean man (patient 2, family FC355), born to healthy nonconsanguineous parents, with normal early motor milestones who developed gait and balance problems at age 13 and walked with short leg braces from age 20. At 22 years he had distal muscle weakness and atrophy, flat feet, atrophy of intrinsic hand, foot and calf muscles, vibration and position sense more disturbed than pain and touch, and absent deep tendon reflexes; he had no other features of Navajo neurohepatopathy and only slightly elevated serum lactate (1.9 mmol/L).
quotes: At age 13, he first felt gait and balance problems. He began to walk with short leg braces at 20 years of age.
Bilateral flat feet, and atrophic changes of intrinsic hand, foot and calf muscles were also noted (Fig. 2d).
Deep tendon reflexes, in all extremities, were absent. He did not present with other phenotypes of NNH. Laboratory findings were normal except for a slightly elevated serum lactate (1.9 mmol/L).

findings.statement: Choi et al. (2015) found similar electrophysiologic results in both patients: sural sensory nerve action potentials were lost early in the disease, median and ulnar motor conduction velocities and CMAPs were decreased, peroneal and tibial CMAPs were not elicited, and no sensory responses were obtained; visual and brainstem auditory evoked potentials were normal. Lower leg MRI showed severe atrophy and fatty replacement predominantly of the soleus muscles with relative sparing of tibialis posterior and lateral gastrocnemius, consistent with length-dependent axonal degeneration and similar to CMT2A; brain MRI was normal.
quotes: Sensory-nerve action potentials of the sural nerve were lost in the early stage of the disease. MCVs and CMAPs were decreased in median and ulnar nerves and CMAPs of peroneal and tibial nerves were not elicited. SCVs and SNAPs were not elicited in either patient.

Lower calf muscle MRIs showed predominant and severe muscle atrophies and fatty replacements in the soleus muscles of both patients; however, the tibialis posterior and lateral gastrocnemius muscles were relatively sparing (Fig. 3c and d).
Brain MRI did not reveal any abnormality in either patient.

phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased amplitude of sensory action potentials
Decreased compound muscle action potential amplitude

findings.statement: Choi et al. (2015) found that sural nerve biopsy from patient 1 at age 34 showed almost complete loss of large and medium-sized myelinated fibers (10/mm2) with a few remaining small myelinated fibers, atrophy and vesicular changes in unmyelinated axons, and no demyelination, remyelination, or onion bulbs. Vastus lateralis biopsy in patient 2 at age 22 showed increased irregular NADH-TR and SDH reaction, a few ragged red fibers, and subsarcolemmal accumulation of enlarged mitochondria.
quotes: Semithin transverse sections from the left distal sural nerve biopsy, from patient 1, showed several remaining small myelinated fibers (MFs) with complete loss (10/mm2) of large and medium-sized MFs
There was no evidence of demyelination, remyelination or onion bulb formation (Fig. 4b).

modified Gomori trichrome stain (data not shown) showed a few ragged, red fibers. Electron microscopic examination showed myofibers with focal subsarcolemmal accumulation of enlarged mitochondria and abnormal membranous structure

phenotypes.text: loss of large myelinated fibers on sural nerve biopsy
phenotypes.hpo_label: Decreased number of large peripheral myelinated nerve fibers
Subsarcolemmal accumulations of abnormally shaped mitochondria

findings.statement: In 2 unrelated Korean patients with autosomal recessive axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy without liver or brain involvement, Choi et al. (2015) identified by whole-exome sequencing a homozygous c.122G-A transition in the MPV17 gene, resulting in an arg41-to-gln (R41Q) substitution at a conserved residue. The mutation was confirmed by Sanger sequencing, a mutant allele was putatively inherited from each parent, and it was absent from 300 controls, in-house exomes (n = 302), dbSNP142, and 1000 Genomes, but present at very low frequency in ESP (0.00008) and ExAC (0.00002471).
quotes: After filtering the WES data for 3 members in each family (Fig. 1), a novel homozygous mutation c.122G> A (p.R41Q) in MPV17 was identified in both families (Fig. 1b). A mutant allele was putatively inherited from each parent in both families.
The mutation was not observed in the 300 controls and in-house exome data (n = 302).

However, this mutation was reported in the Exome Sequencing Project database (http://evs.gs.washington.edu/EVS/) and ExAc browser (http://exac.broadinstitute.org/) with very low allele frequency (0.00008 and 0.00002471, respectively).

findings.statement: Choi et al. (2015) found that knockdown of Mpv17 in NSC34 mouse motor neuronal cells significantly reduced cell proliferation and viability against reactive oxygen species and affected OXPHOS levels, and that overexpression of the R41Q mutant protein significantly inhibited cell proliferation compared to controls, as did R50Q and L143* mutants. They suggested that both loss of normal MPV17 function and gain of detrimental effects of the mutant protein might affect neuronal function.
quotes: knockdown of MPV17 significantly reduced the cell proliferation (Fig. 5b) and viability against ROS in mouse motor neuronal cells (Fig. 5c).
Expression of p.R41Q mutant protein significantly inhibited cell proliferation when compared to controls (Fig. 5e).
These results imply that both the loss of normal function of MPV17 and the gain of detrimental effects of the mutant protein might affect neuronal function.

findings.statement: Choi et al. (2015) noted that, unlike previously described Navajo neurohepatopathy patients in whom neuropathy was always associated with hepatopathy or brain involvement, their patients had only axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy at ages 34 and 22 years. Noting a milder phenotype in patients with an R41W mutation at the same residue, and that R41W overexpression also affected cellular proliferation, they suggested that mutation at arg41 predominantly causes peripheral neuropathy.
quotes: But, the present two patients showed only axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, and they did not exhibit any liver or brain abnormalities, at the ages of 34 and 22 years.
Thus these data implicate that mutation at Arg41 predominantly cause peripheral neuropathy.

relevance_reason: Case report of an adult-onset axonal sensorimotor neuropathy with leukoencephalopathy caused by a homozygous MPV17 mutation, with multiple mtDNA deletions in muscle. This directly characterizes the CMT2EE phenotype.

findings.statement: Blakely et al. (2012) reported a 21-year-old Pakistani man, born to nonconsanguineous parents, who developed walking difficulties at age 14 years. Over several years these progressed to bilateral foot drop requiring orthoses, along with distal numbness. On examination he had distal muscle wasting and weakness, clawed toes, areflexia, distal sensory loss, and mild hepatomegaly; he had no pes cavus and no significant cognitive impairment. Nerve conduction studies showed an axonal sensorimotor polyneuropathy, and sural nerve biopsy showed a severe chronic axonal neuropathy.
quotes: The patient is a 21 year-old Pakistani male, born to non-consanguineous parents.
He first developed neurological symptoms at age 14 years, with gradual onset of walking difficulties that progressed over several years to bilateral foot drops requiring orthoses.
Nerve conduction studies confirmed an axonal sensory motor polyneuropathy and sural nerve biopsy showed a severe chronic axonal neuropathy with only occasional surviving myelinated axons.

phenotypes.text: distal muscle wasting of hands and lower limbs

findings.statement: In the patient reported by Blakely et al. (2012), cranial MRI showed diffuse T2-hyperintense signal in the cerebral and cerebellar white matter, which the authors judged suggestive of leukoencephalopathy; an MRI at age 9 years had been normal. CSF protein (1963 mg/L) and CSF lactate (4.3 mmol/L) were raised. Liver biopsy showed patchy steatosis with early bridging fibrosis, but the patient had no clinically significant chronic liver disease.
quotes: Cranial MRI revealed diffuse hyperintense T2 weighted signal in the cerebral white matter (Fig. 1) and cerebellum, but imaging of the brain stem was normal.
CSF analysis showed an increased protein of 1963 mg/L (normal <500 mg/L) and raised lactate of 4.3 mmol/L (normal 0.7–2.0 mmol/L).
liver biopsy confirmed patchy steatosis (∼20%) with early bridging fibrosis, but overall clinically there was no significant chronic liver disease

findings.statement: Blakely et al. (2012) reported that the proband's sister developed a progressive, fatal hepatitis at age 9 years. Their father had an episode of hepatitis in childhood and recovered fully.
quotes: The patient’s sister developed a progressive, fatal hepatitis at age 9 years. Their father had suffered an episode of hepatitis as a child but made a full recovery.

findings.statement: In the patient's skeletal muscle, Blakely et al. (2012) found about 1% ragged-red fibers and about 20% COX-deficient fibers in a mosaic pattern. Electron microscopy showed abnormal mitochondria with paracrystalline inclusions. mtDNA copy number in muscle was normal, but long-range PCR showed multiple mtDNA deletions, and single-fiber analysis showed clonally expanded mtDNA deletions in COX-deficient fibers.
quotes: Significant mitochondrial respiratory chain deficiency was confirmed following sequential COX–SDH histochemistry which identified ∼20% COX-deficient fibres throughout the biopsy, implicating mtDNA involvement (Fig. 2d).

Real-time PCR demonstrated a normal mtDNA copy number in muscle, whilst common mtDNA point mutations were excluded. Long-range PCR amplification showed the presence of multiple mtDNA deletions (Fig. 3a), confirming a disorder of mtDNA maintenance.
Electron microscopy demonstrated focal subsarcolemmal accumulation of abnormal mitochondria with typical parking lot-like inclusions in some of the enlarged mitochondria (Fig. 2e).

findings.statement: Blakely et al. (2012) sequenced the POLG, DGUOK, and MPV17 genes in the patient and identified a homozygous missense mutation in MPV17, reported as c.2898C>T (c.298C>T in the figure legend), resulting in p.Pro98Leu. This mutation had previously been reported as recessive in a patient with mtDNA depletion in liver, and it affects a residue conserved from human to yeast. Parental samples were not available. The authors suggested the parents, who were of the same Asian ethnicity, shared a common ancestor.
quotes: Sequencing of three genes (POLG, DGUOK and MPV17) implicated in mtDNA maintenance disorders with hepatocerebral involvement revealed a homozygous missense variant (c.2898C>T; p.Pro98Leu) in MPV17 which has previously been reported as a recessive mutation associated with mtDNA depletion in liver (Fig. 3c)
Sequence chromatogram highlighting the c.298C>T (p.Pro98Leu) MPV17 mutation identified in our patient.
unfortunately, parental samples were not available to confirm carrier status.

findings.statement: Blakely et al. (2012) concluded that MPV17 mutation can cause clonally expanded multiple mtDNA deletions and focal COX deficiency in skeletal muscle, as well as mtDNA depletion. They suggested that the MPV17 protein is involved in both mtDNA replication and repair, and is associated with both quantitative and qualitative mtDNA abnormalities.
quotes: we identified multiple mtDNA deletions in skeletal muscle, a finding not previously noted in patients with MPV17 mutations.
we confirm this protein as being intimately involved in both the mtDNA replication and repair processes and associated with both quantitative and qualitative mtDNA abnormalities.
